text:
Nikita Nesterenko found the five-hole on Semyon Varlamov on Saturday, his fourth goal of the season, though it came in a loss to the Islanders. A week earlier he'd sealed a win in Calgary with an empty-netter. Not bad for a 2019 sixth-round pick who plays about 11 minutes a night.

Those minutes are worth more than they look. Anaheim has had 56.6% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Nesterenko on the ice, almost 14 points better than without him, and his own chances, 1.11 expected goals per 60 minutes, are strong for a bottom-six forward. His 4 goals sit right about where those chances say they should. He also hits (47 in 18 games) and skates, with top speed in the 97th percentile. Evolving-Hockey's small sample from last season agreed with the eye test, putting him in the 90th percentile at taking chances away against tough competition, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (8 games) had him as a dump-and-chase forward. He played 12.9 minutes on Saturday; what we'd watch is whether that becomes the norm.
headline: Nesterenko keeps earning more than ten minutes
